# Acceptance test plan

*The checks that decide whether the app works as specified – on the reference TV before each release, and on a port's TV
before the port is called done. An AI coding agent walks a person through it; nobody needs technical knowledge to do the
tests.*

## 0. How to use this plan

**For the agent.**

- **When:** at the end of the port (all of section 1–6), at the exit of each phase (the areas of that phase), and **whenever
  you are unsure** whether something behaves as specified – a quick test with the human is cheaper than a wrong guess.
- **Prepare first:** install the latest build, have the log channel running, and check section 1 with the human. Decide
  which tests do not apply (feature not offered on this TV, no pointer remote, no colour keys …) and tell the human up front;
  record them as `n/a` with the reason in `REQUIREMENTS.md`.
- **Translate the keys.** The steps use the key names of the reference remote (table below). Before you read a step out,
  replace each key with the key or button of *this* TV from the key map in `PLATFORM.md`. If a key does not exist, use the
  replacement your port offers (a button, the ⋯ menu, a long press) and say so.
- **One test at a time:** read the "Before you start" line, help the human get there, then read the steps one by one and
  wait for the answer. Don't rush, don't use jargon, and never ask for passwords, tokens or PINs in the chat.
- **Record** every result (pass / fail / n/a + the human's words) in `REQUIREMENTS.md` and the state file. A failed test:
  fix it, then repeat that test **and** the smoke test (section 2).
- The checks marked "checked by the agent" are yours alone (unit tests, logs, network capture, benchmark). Do them before you
  ask the human for the matching area. Where a test shows the spec's acceptance criterion and that criterion names unit
  tests, those tests are yours too – the human part only covers what can be seen on the TV.

**For the person doing the tests.** You need the TV, its remote, a phone or computer with another Plex app (to compare),
and about two to three hours for the full plan – it can be split over several days. The smoke test takes ten minutes.
Nothing you do here can damage the TV or your Plex server. If a step is unclear, say so – that is useful feedback too.
Tick the boxes or simply tell the agent what you saw.

**For the reference app's own releases.** Before every release, run section 1 (short), section 2, the areas of section 3
that the release changed, and section 4 on the reference TV; record the results in the release notes of the TV test.

**Key names used in the steps** (reference remote):

| Name in the steps | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ▲ ▼ ◀ ▶ | Arrow keys |
| OK | The centre key (select) |
| Back | RETURN / Back key – goes back one step |
| Red, Green, Yellow, Blue | The colour keys (also labelled A, B, C, D) |
| INFO, TOOLS | Info key and the menu key (TOOLS opens the ⋯ menu of the highlighted item) |
| PLAY, PAUSE, STOP, FF, RW | Media keys (FF / RW = fast-forward / rewind) |
| CH▲ / CH▼ | Channel up / down |
| 0–9 | Number keys |

## 1. Device setup checklist

Go through this with the agent before the first test. Tick what is ready; anything missing just means some tests will be
marked `n/a`.

**TV and remote**

- [ ] The TV is switched on, connected to the same home network as the Plex server, and the latest build of the app is installed.
- [ ] You know the TV's exact model (from its *About* or *Support* page) and have told the agent.
- [ ] The TV's own time is correct (or set to network time).
- [ ] The remote has batteries; you know whether it has colour keys, number keys and a pointer (like a "magic" or "smart" remote).

**Plex Media Server**

- [ ] The server is on, up to date, and plays fine in another Plex app.
- [ ] In the server settings, *intro and credits detection* has run for at least one show (needed for the skip tests).
- [ ] Another Plex app (phone app or the Plex web app) is at hand to compare watched states and positions.
- [ ] You know how to switch the server off and on again, or how to unplug its network cable (for the offline tests).

**Test content** – the agent helps you find suitable titles in your library and writes them down:

- [ ] a movie you have started but not finished, and one you have never started
- [ ] a show with at least two seasons, partly watched, with intro markers
- [ ] a title with several audio languages and subtitles (text subtitles; ideally also styled ASS and picture-based subtitles)
- [ ] a title that the TV cannot play directly (the agent tells you which one) – for the conversion tests
- [ ] a movie with two versions (for example 1080p and 4K) and a movie with chapters
- [ ] a library with a collection; a library with more than 100 titles
- [ ] *(optional)* a music library with albums, an audiobook library, an anime title

**Profiles and extras**

- [ ] your main profile; *(optional)* a second adult profile, a kids profile, and a PIN on the main profile
- [ ] *(optional)* a server a friend shared with you, a pointer remote, the helper (only where the TV cannot reach plex.tv itself)

**For the measurements:** a phone with a stopwatch, and a note or chat window to write down results.

## 2. Regression smoke test (10 minutes)

A quick walk through the most important paths. Run it after every fix, before every release and whenever the agent asks.
If one step fails, stop and tell the agent the step number.

1. **Start the app.** It shows your Home screen within a few seconds, with pictures (PERF-4, HOME-3).
2. **Move around Home:** ▶ along a row, ▼ to the next rows. The highlight moves smoothly and the top area changes to the
   highlighted title when you stop (HOME-1, PERF-1).
3. **Open a library** from the sidebar (◀ at the left edge). Scroll down a few rows, then press Back until you are on Home
   again – one step per press (NAV-5, NAV-8).
4. **Open a movie's details**, then press Back: you are on the same card as before (NAV-6).
5. **Play a started title** from *Continue watching*: it offers to resume and starts within a few seconds (PLAY-1, PERF-5).
6. **Seek:** press ▶ three times – the bar shows the target, one jump follows (PLAY-22). Press **OK**: the controls appear;
   wait five seconds, they disappear (PLAY-23).
7. **Audio and subtitles:** press Green, switch the subtitles on, then off again (PLAY-13).
8. **Stop** with Back (twice if the controls are visible). You are back where you started; the position is saved – check
   it in another Plex app (PLAY-7).
9. **Mark something watched** with Yellow and undo it with Yellow again (DET-4).
10. **Search** (Blue or the sidebar): type three letters of a title you own – results appear (SRCH-1).
11. **Change a setting** (for example the clock) and change it back – the change shows at once (A14).
12. *(If you have several profiles)* **switch profile** and back: each profile has its own Home (PROF-4).
13. *(If you have music)* **play an album**, go to Home – the mini player shows and the music keeps playing (MUS-7).
14. **Exit:** press Back on Home until "Exit …?" appears; choose Exit. Start the app again – it opens quickly where you
    left off (NAV-5, HOME-3).

- [ ] All steps passed
- [ ] Failed at step: ___ – what happened:

### A1 Purpose and principles

#### PRIN-2 · The highlight is easy to find

*Spec:* [PRIN-2](SPEC.md#a1-purpose-and-principles)

**Before you start:** Home is open; you sit where you normally watch TV.

1. Look away from the TV while someone else presses ▶ twice (or press it yourself without looking).
2. Look back and find the highlighted card.
3. Do the same in a library and in Settings.

**You should see:** Exactly one highlighted element in the accent colour, found in about a second, on every screen.

**Tell the agent:** Screens where finding the highlight took longer, or where two things looked highlighted.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

### A3 Navigation and focus

#### NAV-1 · Everything works with arrows, OK and Back

*Spec:* [NAV-1](SPEC.md#a31-input-devices)

**Before you start:** Home is open. Put the remote's special keys aside in your mind: use only the arrows, OK and Back.

1. Open a movie's details and start it with the Play button.
2. Show the player controls with OK and open "Audio & subtitles" from the buttons.
3. Leave the player and mark an episode as watched through the ⋯ button or menu.
4. Open Search from the sidebar.

**You should see:** Every function can be reached without colour, number or media keys.

**Tell the agent:** Any function you could only reach with a special key.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-2 · Pointer remote

*Spec:* [NAV-2](SPEC.md#a31-input-devices)

**Before you start:** Only for TVs with a pointer remote (otherwise mark n/a). Home is open.

1. Point at a card: it is highlighted.
2. Click: it opens; press Back.
3. Press and hold the click on a card for about a second: the ⋯ menu opens.
4. Point at the right end of a row and keep still: the row starts scrolling, slowly first, then faster.
5. Click an entry in the hint bar at the bottom right: it does what that key does.
6. Press an arrow key: the highlight follows the key, and the pointer only takes over again when you move it.

**You should see:** Pointing never makes a list run away under the pointer; scrolling happens only at the edges.

**Tell the agent:** Anything that felt jumpy, too fast or too slow.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-3 · Volume belongs to the TV

*Spec:* [NAV-3](SPEC.md#a31-input-devices)

**Before you start:** Home is open; later a video is playing.

1. Press volume up, volume down and mute on Home.
2. Do the same during playback.

**You should see:** The TV's own volume display; the app does nothing else.

**Tell the agent:** Whether volume or mute ever did something inside the app.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-4 · Colour keys always mean the same

*Spec:* [NAV-4](SPEC.md#a33-colour-keys)

**Before you start:** A library with movies is open. If the remote has no colour keys, the agent tells you the buttons that replace them.

1. On a movie press Yellow: a message says it is marked watched. Press Yellow again to undo.
2. Press Blue: Search opens; press Back.
3. Press Red: "Sort & filter" opens; press Back.
4. Open a movie's details and press Green: "Audio & subtitles" opens.
5. Start the movie, press Yellow (chapters) and Blue (sleep timer).

**You should see:** Yellow = watched, Blue = search, Green = audio & subtitles, Red = the screen's main action; in the player Yellow = chapters, Blue = sleep timer.

**Tell the agent:** Any colour key that did something else, or nothing.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-5 · Back goes back one step at a time

*Spec:* [NAV-5](SPEC.md#a34-return-chains) · *Acceptance criterion:* from every screen, pressing RETURN repeatedly ends at the exit dialog without skipping a level.

**Before you start:** Home is open.

1. Go to the third row, fourth card, and press Back: the highlight jumps to the first card of the first row.
2. Press Back again: the sidebar opens.
3. Press Back again: "Exit …?" appears with Cancel highlighted; choose Cancel.
4. Open a library, go down three rows and press Back three times: first row, then sidebar, then Home.
5. In Settings open a category, go to a row, press Back twice: category, then sidebar.

**You should see:** Every press goes back exactly one step and nothing is skipped; you always end at the exit question.

**Tell the agent:** The screen where Back skipped a step or did nothing.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-6 · Screens remember where you were

*Spec:* [NAV-6](SPEC.md#a35-focus-memory-and-focus-after-changes)

**Before you start:** Home is open.

1. In the second row move to the fifth card.
2. Go down one row and up again: you are on the fifth card.
3. Open that card's details and press Back: same card.
4. Open details, then an actor, then a title, and press Back three times.

**You should see:** Each step back lands on exactly the element you left.

**Tell the agent:** Where the highlight landed somewhere else.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-7 · The highlight never points at nothing

*Spec:* [NAV-7](SPEC.md#a35-focus-memory-and-focus-after-changes)

**Before you start:** *Continue watching* has at least three titles; a show is partly watched.

1. In Continue watching highlight the second card and press Yellow: the card disappears and the highlight moves to the card that took its place. Press Yellow to undo.
2. Play an episode from the show's details for 30 seconds and stop: you are back on that episode.
3. Switch to another profile and back: Home starts at the first card of the first row.

**You should see:** After every change the highlight is on a sensible element.

**Tell the agent:** Any moment when no element was highlighted.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-8 · Sidebar

*Spec:* [NAV-8](SPEC.md#a36-sidebar) · *Acceptance criterion:* RIGHT closes and restores the content focus; OK on the current page only closes.

**Before you start:** Home is open.

1. Press ◀ at the left edge: the sidebar opens wide and marks Home.
2. Press ▶: it closes and the highlight is back where it was.
3. Open it again and press OK on Home: it only closes.
4. Open it, move to a library and press OK: the library opens.
5. Check the order: profile at the top, then Search, Discover, Home, your libraries, Settings at the bottom.

**You should see:** The sidebar opens and closes quickly; the current page is marked.

**Tell the agent:** Anything missing or in a different order.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-9 · Hint bar

*Spec:* [NAV-9](SPEC.md#a37-hint-bar-toast-dialog-panel)

**Before you start:** Home is open.

1. Look at the bottom right on Home, in a library, in details and in the paused player.
2. Open a ⋯ menu and look again.

**You should see:** At most five hints; colour keys as coloured squares (A–D); the hints match what the keys do and change for the menu.

**Tell the agent:** A hint that did not match what the key did.

- [ ] Pass

#### NAV-14 · Hint bar: always, briefly, off

*Spec:* [NAV-14](SPEC.md#a37-hint-bar-toast-dialog-panel)

**Before you start:** Home is open.

1. Settings › Display › "Button hints" = Briefly; go back to Home and wait 5 s.
2. Press TOOLS, then Back.
3. Set "Off"; open Home, a library and pause a video.
4. Open Help & info › Remote control keys.
5. Set "Always" again.

**You should see:** 1) The bar appears and fades out after about 4 s. 2) It comes back with the menu. 3) No bar anywhere, not even in the paused video, and the keys still work. 4) Every key you saw in a hint bar is listed there. 5) The bar stays.

**Tell the agent:** Where the bar did not hide or come back.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-10 · Short messages

*Spec:* [NAV-10](SPEC.md#a37-hint-bar-toast-dialog-panel)

**Before you start:** A library is open.

1. Mark a title watched with Yellow: a message appears.
2. Try to move the highlight onto the message.
3. Wait.
4. In Settings › Diagnostics choose “Delete log”: the message appears below the grey description box.

**You should see:** The message cannot be highlighted, never covers text and disappears by itself after a few seconds (about 6 with an undo hint).

**Tell the agent:** Messages that stayed, overlapped or were cut off.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-11 · Questions (dialogs)

*Spec:* [NAV-11](SPEC.md#a37-hint-bar-toast-dialog-panel)

**Before you start:** Home is open.

1. Press Back until "Exit …?" appears: Cancel is highlighted.
2. Press Back: the question closes, the app stays open.
3. On a show's details highlight a season and press Yellow: a question with the number of episodes appears, Cancel highlighted. Choose Cancel.

**You should see:** The safe choice is always highlighted; Back always cancels.

**Tell the agent:** A question where a risky choice was highlighted.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### NAV-12 · Selection panels

*Spec:* [NAV-12](SPEC.md#a37-hint-bar-toast-dialog-panel)

**Before you start:** A library is open.

1. Press Red: a panel opens on the right.
2. Choose a sort order with OK: the panel closes and the order changes.
3. Open the genre filter (a long list): the list scrolls while the highlight stays near the fourth row.
4. In Settings open a list where you can tick several entries: OK ticks, Back closes and applies.
5. On a settings row press INFO: a help text opens; INFO, OK or Back closes it.
6. In Discover open a title with a very long name and a long description and press INFO: the title stays on one line ending with “…”, the text ends above the hint bar with “…”.

**You should see:** Panels open without animation and behave the same everywhere; no text runs off the panel.

*Spec:* [NAV-13](SPEC.md#a37-hint-bar-toast-dialog-panel)

2. In Search type "xqzv".

### A4 Start, profiles and PINs

#### PROF-1 · Signing in

*Spec:* [PROF-1](SPEC.md#a41-two-connection-modes)

**Before you start:** The app is installed but not signed in yet. The agent tells you which way your TV signs in (code on the TV, or the setup program on a computer).

1. Start the app.
2. Follow the instructions on the screen or of the setup program.
3. Type your password only on the plex.tv page in a browser.
4. Choose your profile.

**You should see:** Your libraries appear. The TV and the agent never asked for your password.

**Tell the agent:** Which way you signed in, and any step that was confusing.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### PROF-2 · Which profile the app starts in

*Spec:* [PROF-2](SPEC.md#a42-start-rules) · *Acceptance criterion:* unit tests for each branch; kids profile + PIN switch on → app starts in the kids profile.

**Before you start:** Signed in. Some steps need several profiles or a kids profile – skip those you don't have.

1. Close and restart the app: it opens as set in Settings › Start profile (default: main profile, straight to Home).
2. Set Start profile to "Show profile picker" and restart: the picker appears.
3. Set it to "Last used", use a profile without a PIN, restart: that profile opens.
4. With a kids profile and "Profile switch needs PIN" on: switch to the kids profile and restart – the app starts in the kids profile.

**You should see:** The app always starts in the profile the setting describes.

**Tell the agent:** A restart that opened a different profile than expected.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### PROF-4 · Each profile has its own content and settings

*Spec:* [PROF-4](SPEC.md#a42-start-rules)

**Before you start:** Two profiles.

1. Switch from your profile to the other one.
2. Look at Home: that profile's own Continue watching; all pictures load.
3. Change a setting there (for example switch "Show clock" off).
4. Switch back to your profile.

**You should see:** Each profile shows its own titles; the setting changed only in the other profile.

**Tell the agent:** Content or settings that leaked from one profile into the other.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### PROF-5 · PIN pad and lockout

*Spec:* [PROF-5](SPEC.md#a43-pins)

**Before you start:** A profile with a PIN.

1. In the profile picker choose that profile.
2. Enter a wrong PIN five times.
3. Press Back and choose the profile again.
4. When the countdown has ended, enter the right PIN.

**You should see:** After the fifth wrong try a 30-second lock with a countdown, still running after reopening; the right PIN opens the profile right after the fourth digit, without OK.

**Tell the agent:** Whether the lock could be skipped.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### PROF-6 · App PIN

*Spec:* [PROF-6](SPEC.md#a43-pins)

**Before you start:** Only if your port uses the setup-file mode (the agent tells you; otherwise n/a). Main profile.

1. Settings › Profile & account › "PINs of all profiles": set a PIN for a profile (enter it twice).
2. Switch to that profile: the PIN is asked.
3. Restart the app and switch again.

**You should see:** The PIN is asked every time; a short spinner shows while it is checked.

**Tell the agent:** How long the check took.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### PROF-7 · Kids can't leave their profile without the PIN

*Spec:* [PROF-7](SPEC.md#a43-pins)

**Before you start:** The main profile has a PIN and a kids profile exists.

1. Settings › Profile & account › "Profile switch needs PIN": on.
2. Switch to the kids profile.
3. Open the profile entry at the top of the sidebar.
4. Press Back.

**You should see:** The main profile's PIN is asked; Back keeps you in the kids profile.

**Tell the agent:** Any way out of the kids profile without the PIN.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

*Spec:* [PROF-8](SPEC.md#a43-pins)

**Before you start:** A kids profile exists and the main profile has no PIN.

2. When "Protect adult profiles?" appears, choose "Later".

### A5 Home

#### HOME-1 · Home layout

*Spec:* [HOME-1](SPEC.md#a5-home)

**Before you start:** Home is open; the agent shows you `home.png` for comparison.

1. Compare the screen with the reference picture.
2. Move along a row and stop: after a short moment the top area shows the highlighted title.
3. Move quickly: the top area waits until you stop.
4. Move down several rows.

**You should see:** Big picture and text on top, rows below; the highlighted row stays at the same height and the rows slide under it.

**Tell the agent:** Differences from the reference picture.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### HOME-2 · Home rows

*Spec:* [HOME-2](SPEC.md#a5-home)

**Before you start:** Home is open; another Plex app at hand.

1. Check the rows: Continue watching, Next episodes, and "New in …" for each movie and show library.
2. Compare them with the same rows in the other Plex app.

**You should see:** The same titles in the same order; in "New in …" each show only once.

**Tell the agent:** Rows that are missing, or titles that differ.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### HOME-3 · Home appears at once from the cache

*Spec:* [HOME-3](SPEC.md#a5-home) · *Acceptance criterion:* cold start with cache shows content before any network answer; stopping an episode halfway and returning to Home keeps it in Continue watching (first, with the new progress).

**Before you start:** The app was used before.

1. Close and restart the app: Home appears immediately with the last content.
2. Switch the Plex server off and restart the app: Home still shows the last content, and a message says the server is not answering. Switch the server on again.
3. Watch a title for a minute and stop: Continue watching is updated.

**You should see:** Content before any waiting; updates follow by themselves.

**Tell the agent:** How long Home took to appear, and anything that was missing.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

*Spec:* [HOME-4](SPEC.md#a5-home)

- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

**You should see:** Undo works for six seconds; afterwards the title is also gone from Continue watching in the other app.

- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

*Spec:* [DET-3](SPEC.md#a7-details)

2. Look at the season tabs (specials come last). With many seasons no tab is cut off: an arrow › at the right edge shows that more seasons follow; move right until it turns into ‹ on the left. 2. Pause it and wait.

**Tell the agent:** Whether a screensaver interrupted the video.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### PLAY-30 · Fine scrubbing on the progress bar

*Spec:* [PLAY-30](SPEC.md#a95-seeking-and-osd)

**Before you start:** Only with a pointer remote (otherwise n/a). Settings → Playback → *Fine scrubbing on the progress bar* switched on, *Fine scrubbing style* left at the default *Panel above the bar*. A movie of about two hours is playing; the agent tells you a target time (for example 1:07:30).

1. Move the pointer onto the progress bar and hold it still for about a second, finger resting on the touchpad.
2. A box with a stretched bar slides up above the controls; move left/right until the time under the small marker shows the target, then click.
3. Do the same 9 more times with other target times; each time note how far the video landed from the target.
4. Point at the bar, read the time for a second and move on – 10 times.
5. **Gap and button guard:** open it again, then on purpose let your thumb drift down over the times and onto the button row while moving left/right, and click there once. Open it again, drift down onto a button and move far to the side, then click.
6. **Gap to the fine bar:** open it and slowly move up from the main bar towards the box and back down several times, the way you would naturally adjust.
7. Open it again and move the pointer up and away; open it again and press Back.
8. Switch *Pointer control* off and look at the setting.

**You should see:** It opens only when you hold still (not while moving along the bar); the time does not jump when it opens; a click jumps once; in at least 9 of 10 tries the video lands within 30 seconds of the target. Step 5: while it is open **no button lights up or reacts** – the click on the button row sets the fine target (the video jumps there, nothing pauses, no menu opens); moving sideways down there only makes the marker stop at the window's end. Step 6: the small up/down wobble of your thumb never closes it; the distance between the main bar and the bar in the box feels like one short, easy movement – neither cramped nor a long way. Moving up above the box or Back closes it (Back keeps the controls); with pointer control off the setting is greyed out.

**Tell the agent:** The 10 distances from the target, how long each try took, how often it opened without you wanting it, **whether any button ever reacted while it was open**, whether the gap in step 6 felt too small or too large, anything that flickered or felt slow.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

#### PLAY-31 · Fine scrubbing styles

*Spec:* [PLAY-31](SPEC.md#a95-seeking-and-osd)

**Before you start:** Only with a pointer remote (otherwise n/a). *Fine scrubbing on the progress bar* is on. An episode with a *Skip intro* button and subtitles, and a two-hour movie; preview images on the server if you have them.

1. Settings → Playback → *Fine scrubbing style*: read the three choices (*Panel above the bar* marked as chosen if you never changed it) and press INFO.
2. With *Panel above the bar*, in the episode, while *Skip intro* shows, rest the pointer on the bar until fine scrubbing opens.
3. Pick *Stretching bar*; open it on the movie and watch the opening.
4. Pick *Filmstrip*; open it on the movie and move left/right across the pictures.
5. Repeat 4 with *Preview images when skipping* switched off.
6. For each style click a target time, then open it again, let the pointer slip down onto the buttons and click there once, then move up and away.

**You should see:** Three choices, no *Fine bar*. Panel: a box slides up out of the top edge of the controls, touching it without overlapping; the two thin slanted lines from the highlighted part of the bar up to the box look alike on both sides, start right on the corners of the highlight and fade out softly towards the box (no hard or jagged ends, also with the pointer at the very start or end of the bar); the hint sits in its top line and never touches the times; subtitles move up; the skip button stays if it is beside the box. Stretching bar: the part under the pointer visibly widens, the rest squeezes aside, and the label below the buttons names the mode. Filmstrip: seven pictures fill in one after the other; the one under the pointer is framed and shows the target. Without preview images it looks like the panel. Every style opens smoothly (no stutter), is equally precise, closes at once, and in step 6 the click on the buttons sets the target instead of pressing a button.

**Tell the agent:** Which style you liked best, anything that overlapped, flickered or felt slow, any button that reacted while fine scrubbing was open, how long the filmstrip pictures took to appear.

- [ ] Pass
- [ ] Fail – what happened instead:

<details><summary>Checked by the agent (3)</summary>

| ID | What | How the agent verifies it |
|---|---|---|
| [PLAY-2](SPEC.md#a91-start-and-decision) | Playback sequence | Request log of a playback: metadata → track choice (PUT only when it differs) → decision (15 s timeout) → direct URL or HLS; unit tests for the sequence |
| [PLAY-3](SPEC.md#a91-start-and-decision) | Decision query and device profile | Unit tests for the decision parameters; the profile extra is built from the device's measured capabilities (`PLATFORM.md`); player matrix (SPEC C3) shows the expected decision per file; no `hasMDE`; bitrate limit only when converting |
| [PLAY-21](SPEC.md#a94-markers-up-next-still-watching-sleep) | "Lower quality?" offer | Unit tests of the offer rule (20 s loading or 2 rebuffers in 60 s, once per video; rebuffers in the first 5 s after start, seek or resume do not count); a throttled-network run shows the button and restarts at the same spot |

</details>

### A15 Text and i18n

#### TXT-2 · Texts are friendly and clear

*Spec:* [TXT-2](SPEC.md#a15-text-and-i18n)

**Before you start:** During all other tests.

1. Whenever you see a setting, read its description below the list.

## 4. Performance measurements

Speed is part of the product (SPEC A17). The **agent** measures the exact numbers with its benchmark (the same scenarios
as the reference, SPEC A17.3); **you** confirm what the numbers cannot show – whether it *feels* fast and smooth from the
sofa. Write both into the results.

**The agent's benchmark run** (about 2–5 minutes): the agent starts it (on the reference TV: press 9, 8, 7 on Home, each
within 4 seconds). The app then presses keys by itself. **Don't touch the remote** until the agent says it is finished.
The agent reads the numbers from the log and compares them with the budgets below.

| Measurement | Budget (SPEC A17.1) | How you observe it | Agent's number | What you saw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Moving the highlight with a key held (Home, Library, Details, Search, player controls) | ≥ 55 frames per second, no frame over 50 ms (PERF-1) | Hold ▶ in a long row and ▼ in a big library for 5 seconds each: does it run evenly, or does it stop and jump? | | |
| Reaction to a single key press | ≤ 100 ms (PERF-3) | Press ▶ once at a time on Home, in Settings and in the player controls: does every press react at once? | | |
| Cold start to first content (with cache) | < 3 s (PERF-4) | Close the app fully. Start the stopwatch when you press the app's tile, stop it when Home shows pictures. | | |
| Player start to moving picture | direct play ≤ 2.5 s, converting ≤ 6 s (PERF-5) | Stopwatch from OK on Play until the picture moves – once for a title that plays directly and once for one that is converted. | | |
| Seek | direct play ≤ 2 s, converting ≤ 5 s (PERF-6) | During playback press 5 (middle of the video); stopwatch until the picture moves again. | | |
| Pictures while scrolling | no stalls during key sequences (PERF-7) | While holding ▼ in a library: the highlight keeps moving even if pictures appear only when you stop. | | |
| Long use | ≤ 10 % memory growth after 2 h (PERF-10) | Leave the app playing a long movie or the screensaver running for 2 hours, then use Home and Library: is it as fast as at the start? | | |

The agent records: the benchmark lines (fps, frames over 50 ms, worst frame, image stalls per scenario), the build tested,
and the device. On fast hardware the budgets are tighter (60 fps, no frame over 33 ms) – never looser.

## 5. Privacy and security checks

Most of these the agent checks itself (network capture, logs, code); a few need you. Details: SPEC A18.

**With you**

- [ ] **Your password was only ever typed on plex.tv** – in a browser or the official link page – never on the TV, never in
  the setup program and never in the chat with the agent (SEC-2).
- [ ] **No secrets in the chat:** the agent never asked for your password, Plex token or PIN. If one appeared anywhere, the
  agent told you to remove the device on plex.tv (*Authorized Devices*) – do that (SEC-3).
- [ ] **Authorized Devices on plex.tv** lists the app (one entry per profile or one for the TV); removing an entry signs only
  that profile out on the TV (SEC-3).
- [ ] **Kids profile:** it cannot reach adult profiles without the PIN, and has no account or diagnostics settings (PROF-7,
  PROF-9).
- [ ] **Diagnostics leave the TV only when you press "Send log"** (NET-5, SEC-8).

**By the agent** (the agent reports the result to you in plain words)

- [ ] **Network capture during 10 minutes of normal use** (start, Home, Library, playback, Search): only your Plex server is
  contacted – plus plex.tv only for sign-in and the optional Discover/watchlist features, and other servers you enabled.
  No analytics, ads or other third parties (SEC-1, PRIN-12).
- [ ] **Logs and storage contain no tokens, PINs or sign-in codes** – the agent searches the log and the app's storage for
  them (NET-5, SEC-3).
- [ ] **Tokens are kept in the platform's secure storage** where it has one, and sent as headers rather than in URLs where
  the player allows it (SEC-3).
- [ ] **Home-network rules:** plain HTTP only to private addresses; https preferred where the server offers it (SEC-4).
- [ ] **Helper and setup program** (only if the port uses them): their tests pass unchanged (SEC-5, SEC-6).

## 7. Maintaining this plan

*For maintainers of the reference app.* Section 3 is generated from SPEC.md and the step table below. Every requirement ID
of Part A needs exactly one row: `human` rows are tests with a person (all columns filled, steps numbered `1) … 2) …`,
phrased for someone with a remote and no technical knowledge); `agent` rows say how the agent verifies the requirement on
its own. Add or change a row in the same commit as the spec change, then run `npm run spec`. The check fails if a
requirement has no row or a row names an ID that no longer exists.

<!-- hand:test-steps -->
